2609.14418.title: Surrogate-Assisted Genetic Programming with Phenotypic Characterisation in Dynamic Multi-Mode Project Scheduling
2609.14418.paper_summary: Dynamic multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling requires decisions to be made under precedence constraints, limited resources, multiple execution modes, and uncertain activity durations. Genetic programming (GP) can automatically evolve heuristic rules for such problems, but its simulation-based fitness evaluation is computationally expensive. This study investigates phenotypic characterisation (PC) in surrogate-assisted GP to evolve higher-quality scheduling heuristics under a fixed budget of full simulation-based fitness evaluations. A key question is how GP individuals should be encoded into phenotypic characterisations to support effective fitness estimation. To answer this question, three PC encoding schemes with different levels of information richness are designed: priority-value encoding, which preserves raw rule outputs; rank encoding, which captures candidate ordering; and binary encoding, which represents final scheduling decisions. These encodings are combined with different distance metrics to measure behavioural similarity between GP individuals. The experimental results show that binary encoding with Euclidean distance provides the most effective and robust surrogate guidance. Further analyses show that surrogate estimation accuracy alone does not fully explain the performance differences. The PC representation also determines how effectively phenotypically redundant offspring are removed and how much behavioural diversity is retained after preselection. Ablation experiments further demonstrate that duplicate removal and surrogate preselection provide complementary benefits, with their combination producing the largest improvement. These findings highlight that effective surrogate-assisted GP depends not only on identifying promising offspring, but also on controlling redundancy and preserving useful diversity during evolutionary search.
2609.14418.paper_summary_zh: 動態多模式資源受限的專案排程需要在優先順序約束、有限資源、多種執行模式和不確定的活動持續時間下做出決策。遺傳編程 (GP) 可以自動演化出這類問題的啟發式規則，但其基於模擬的適應度評估計算成本高昂。本研究探討在代理輔助 GP 中的表型特徵化 (PC)，以在固定的全模擬基礎適應度評估預算下演化出更高質量的排程啟發式規則。一個關鍵問題是 GP 個體應如何編碼為表型特徵，以支持有效的適應度估算。為了回答這個問題，設計了三種具有不同信息豐富度的 PC 編碼方案：優先值編碼，保留原始規則輸出；排名編碼，捕捉候選排序；以及二進制編碼，表示最終的排程決策。這些編碼與不同的距離度量相結合，以測量 GP 個體之間的行為相似性。實驗結果顯示，使用歐幾里得距離的二進制編碼提供了最有效且穩健的代理指導。進一步的分析顯示，僅僅依賴代理估算的準確性並不能完全解釋性能差異。PC 表示法還決定了表型冗餘後代被移除的有效性以及在預選後保留的行為多樣性。消融實驗進一步證明，重複移除和代理預選提供了互補的好處，兩者的結合產生了最大的改進。這些發現強調，有效的代理輔助 GP 不僅依賴於識別有前景的後代，還依賴於控制冗餘和在進化搜索過程中保留有用的多樣性。
